version.changelog: v1.1: stuck handling (stop + inform user), delete file on completion, no clutter

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed autonomous task runner, but its trigger is too broad and it can create, update, message about, and delete task-state files without clear explicit opt-in.

dimensions.detail: The capabilities generally match the stated purpose of running multi-step tasks autonomously with a workspace progress file and user updates.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Activation includes any multi-step task where the agent infers autonomous execution is expected, which is materially broader than explicit user opt-in and could enable the workflow unexpectedly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only a single markdown skill file, with no executable scripts, dependencies, or install-time code shown.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Writing a task plan file and running normal task steps are purpose-aligned, but Telegram updates imply outbound messaging behavior without specifying user-controlled setup or limits.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill uses a fixed persistent path at /workspace/memory/ralph-loop.md and later mandates deleting it on completion, which may surprise users or remove useful audit context.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to run multi-step work with minimal questions, write a progress file under /workspace/memory, send Telegram-style progress updates, and delete the working log when done. Prefer using it only with an explicit trigger phrase, and ask to keep or archive the log if you need an audit trail.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad inferred activation rule is not necessary for the skill's purpose; explicit Ralph Loop commands would be sufficient and safer.
[SQP-2] expected: A progress memory file is expected for this workflow, but the fixed path and automatic creation deserve user awareness before use.
[SQP-2] expected: Cleanup of the working file is disclosed and purpose-related, but automatic deletion can remove task history unless the user explicitly asks to keep it.
